title: Exceptional adjunction transport across the etale comparison
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, let $\ell
e p$ be prime, and let $A$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$. Let $f:X	o Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes and fix a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j} ar X\xrightarrow{p_f}Y$, with $ ar X$ separated and of finite type over $k$. Use ordinary module-sheaf derived categories on the small étale and pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories; def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], and comparison pullbacks $
u_T^*$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Let $F_{\mathrm{et}}=Rp_{f,\mathrm{et},*}j^{\mathrm{et}}_!$ and $F_{\mathrm{proet}}=Rp_{f,\mathrm{proet},*}j^{\mathrm{proet}}_!$ be the compact-support composites for this same compactification [def-amb-etale-compact-support; def-sfb-finite-derived-lower-shriek-compactification], and let $f^	imes$ be the ordinary étale right adjoint of $F_{\mathrm{et}}$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Suppose $f^	imes$ preserves bounded constructible [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] finite-Tor [def-kun-tor-amplitude] complexes. Every bounded constructible [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] finite-Tor [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude] pro-étale complex $K$ on $Y$ has bounded constructible finite-Tor étale origin $K_{\mathrm{et}}$. The objects $H_K=
u_X^*f^	imes K_{\mathrm{et}}$ are bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude, naturally in $K$. On $D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ there is a natural comparison isomorphism
$$
u_Y^*F_{\mathrm{et}}\simeq F_{\mathrm{proet}}
u_X^*.$$
For every $M\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ there are natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(
u_X^*M,H_K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_{\mathrm{proet}}
u_X^*M,K),$$
and this bijection sends $h$ to $t_K\circ F_{\mathrm{proet}}(h)$, where $t_K:F_{\mathrm{proet}}H_K	o K$ is the transported ordinary étale counit.

proof.text: A finite ring is Noetherian: every ideal is generated by its finitely many elements. Since a field is Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X,Y,\bar X$ Noetherian; finite type over $k$ gives quasi-compactness, and separatedness gives quasi-separatedness. Thus [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] applies to the discrete ring $A$ and $Y$. Choose a bounded constructible witness $\alpha:\nu_Y^*E\xrightarrow{\sim}K$. If $K$ has Tor interval $[a,b]$, [lem-exc-comparison-tor-interval], applied to the bounded-below complex $E$, implies that $E$ has that same interval. This theorem tests every module sheaf on the respective site, so no restriction to classical test sheaves is being imposed. Set $K_{\mathrm{et}}=E$.

source.place: Final restriction paragraph; detailed ordinary-to-pro-etale transport argument supplied by Q02.

proof.text:
Put $R=f^	imes$. By the assumed preservation, $RE$ is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude. Then $H_K=
u_X^*RE$ is bounded constructible in the global-partition sense of the statement: by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] (3), $\mathcal H^i(H_K)\cong
u_X^*\mathcal H^i(RE)$, so $H_K$ is bounded; take for each $i$ the finite stratification $(\iota_k:Z_k	o X)$ by constructible locally closed strata on which $\iota_k^{-1}\mathcal H^i(RE)$ is finite locally constant; by the pullback clause of [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] (for the morphism $\iota_k$), $\iota_k^*
u_X^*\mathcal H^i(RE)\cong
u_{Z_k}^*\iota_k^{-1}\mathcal H^i(RE)$, and an etale covering trivializing the latter is a pro-etale covering on which $
u_{Z_k}^*$ of the constant sheaf of a finite $A$-module is the constant sheaf of that module, so its stalks are finite. (Conversely, the global partition of $K$ in Step 1 is in particular a local one, so $K$ lies in the category of [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison].) The forward implication of [lem-exc-comparison-tor-interval] preserves its finite Tor interval, including tensor tests against nonclassical pro-etale module sheaves. Choose a quasi-inverse to the constructible comparison equivalence; then $E$ and $H_K$ vary functorially with $K$. The independence of this choice is checked in Step 5.

proof.text:
Write $P=
u_X^*$ and $Q=
u_Y^*$. By [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], the sheaf comparison $
u_{ ar X}^*j^{\mathrm{et}}_!\simeq j^{\mathrm{proet}}_!P$ is natural. All functors in this comparison are exact by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact], [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] and [lem-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero-exact]. Applying it degreewise therefore gives the same natural isomorphism on derived categories, preserving bounded-below inputs. Properness of $p_f$ gives quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness, so [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] applies to $j^{\mathrm{et}}_!M$ for every $M\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Compose its isomorphism $Q Rp_{f,\mathrm{et},*}j^{\mathrm{et}}_!M	o Rp_{f,\mathrm{proet},*}
u_{ ar X}^*j^{\mathrm{et}}_!M$ with the derived open comparison. Two identifications are used here. First, the pro-etale $j_!$ of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] (sheafified extension-by-zero presheaf) is the $j_!$ of [def-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero] with $\mathcal A=\Mod_A$: for an object $V$ of $ ar X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ the indexing category of $\operatorname{Lan}_{\ell^{\mathrm{op}}}F(V)$ has the terminal object $V	o U$ when $V$ factors through $U$ and is empty otherwise, so the two presheaves agree before sheafification. Second, on bounded-below inputs the unbounded K-injective derived direct images of the two definitions agree with the bounded-below ones of [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison]: a bounded-below complex has a bounded-below injective resolution, which is K-injective, so both are computed by it; in particular $Rp_{f,*}$ of a bounded-below complex is bounded below. By [def-amb-etale-compact-support] and [def-sfb-finite-derived-lower-shriek-compactification], this is the required natural isomorphism $ eta:QF_{\mathrm{et}}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{\mathrm{proet}}P$. These comparisons use the given compactification and the constant ring $A$ throughout.

proof.text: For brevity put $F=F_{\mathrm{et}}$ and $G=F_{\mathrm{proet}}$. For $M\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, Step 3 and the witness $\alpha:QE\simeq K$ identify $\operatorname{Hom}(GPM,K)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(QFM,QE)$. The latter is $\operatorname{Hom}(FM,E)$ by [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. Here $FM$ is bounded below: exact $j_!$ preserves the lower bound, and the derived direct image of a bounded-below complex is bounded below (Step 3, computed on a bounded-below injective resolution), as also recorded in the $D^+$ range of [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison]. The schemes are Noetherian by Step 1, $A$ is finite, and $p_f$ is proper of finite type, so [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] supplies $F\dashv R$ in the ordinary etale categories. Its Hom bijection identifies this with $\operatorname{Hom}(M,RE)$, which is $\operatorname{Hom}(PM,PRE)$ by [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] on $X$; $RE$ is bounded by Step 2. Reversing these bijections proves the asserted Hom bijection. All the maps are natural in $M$ and $E$.

source.place: Final restriction paragraph; detailed ordinary-to-pro-etale transport argument supplied by Q02.

proof.text: If $\alpha':QE'\simeq K'$ is another witness and $v:K\to K'$ is a morphism, full faithfulness in [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] gives a unique $u:E\to E'$ with $Q(u)=\alpha'^{-1}v\alpha$. Send $v$ to $P R(u)$. Uniqueness shows that identity morphisms and composites lift to identities and composites. For two witnesses of the same $K$, lift $\alpha'^{-1}\alpha$ and its inverse; their composites lift identity morphisms and hence are identities. This gives the unique compatible isomorphism between the corresponding $H_K$. Naturality of $\beta$ and of the ordinary Hom bijection then conjugates the chain of Step 4 by exactly these isomorphisms. Thus that chain is natural in $K$ and independent of the witness up to its canonical isomorphism.

source.place: Final restriction paragraph; detailed ordinary-to-pro-etale transport argument supplied by Q02.

proof.text:
Let $\varepsilon:FR\to\mathrm{id}$ be the counit of the ordinary adjunction [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. With $\beta:QF\simeq GP$ as in Step 3, define explicitly
$$t_K=\alpha\circ Q(\varepsilon_E)\circ\beta_{RE}^{-1}:GPRE\longrightarrow K.$$
For $h:PM\to PRE$, full faithfulness [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] gives a unique $u:M\to RE$ with $h=P(u)$. The forward direction of the chain in Step 4 sends $h$ to
$$\alpha\circ Q(\varepsilon_E\circ F(u))\circ\beta_M^{-1}.$$
Naturality of $\beta^{-1}$ says $QF(u)\circ\beta_M^{-1}=\beta_{RE}^{-1}\circ GP(u)$. Substitution makes this composite exactly $t_K\circ G(h)$, as required. For a witness map $u:E\to E'$, counit naturality $\varepsilon_{E'}\circ FR(u)=u\circ\varepsilon_E$, together with naturality of $\beta^{-1}$, gives $t_{K'}\circ G(PR(u))=v\circ t_K$. For witness isomorphisms from Step 5 this is precisely compatibility with changing the witness. This proves the stated transported counit formula without assuming an ambient pro-etale right adjoint.
